REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - FEBRUARY 25, 2016 - CITY HALL -
7:00 P.M.
COUNCIL CHAMBERS, BLOOMFIELD AVENUE AT 183RD STREET
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. In addition, requests may be made of the staff for reports which will be presented to the City Council at a subsequent meeting, or for the scheduling of future agenda items. There will be no discussion or action taken on any of the items that may be presented during this agenda item.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON
FEBRUARY 25, 2016, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Councilmember Ray.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by the Cerritos Recreation Services Division Youth
  Basketball League Girls Rookie III team “Snowflakes”.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Mark E. Pulido
  Council/Agency Member Naresh Solanki
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair George Ray
  Mayor/Chair Carol Chen

5.  Presentations/Appointments

  Proclamations were presented as follows:

  Dr. Philip Kress, DDS (Business Spotlight)

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  None.

7.  Consent Calendar
  Items under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by
  one motion. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless a
  Council/Agency Member or citizen so requests, in which event the item will be
  removed from the Consent Calendar and considered separately.

7A.  Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated February 25,
  2016 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to approve the Register
  of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated February 25, 2016 in the total amount of
  $3,205,455.69 (COUNCIL). The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray, Chen
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  February 25, 2016
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 2 of 6

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7B.  Approval of the Register of Demands for the Successor Agency to the Cerritos
  Redevelopment Agency dated February 25, 2016 (SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to approve the Register
  of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated February 25, 2016 in the total amount of
  $4,481.00 (SUCCESSOR AGENCY). The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray, Chen
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7C.  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of February
  11, 2016 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of February 11, 2016
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY). The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray, Chen
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

8A.  Review and consideration of the City of Cerritos Hazard Mitigation Plan Draft
  (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Rebecca Scott, Management Analyst. A PowerPoint
  Presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments.

  Dr. Mark Chung spoke in support of the plan.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed
  public comments and the public hearing.

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Solanki, to authorize staff to
  finalize the City of Cerritos Hazard Mitigation Plan draft and submit it to the California
  Office of Emergency Services and FEMA. The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray, Chen
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  February 25, 2016
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 3 of 6

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8B.  Review and consideration of a request for authorization for the City of Cerritos
  (Seller) to sell City-owned property and related improvements located at 13043
  166th Street, Cerritos, California, 90703, to Fabric Town (Buyer), pursuant to
  terms of a Letter of Intent (LOI). The subject property is zoned Development
  Area One (ADP-1) and is located within the Cerritos Industrial Park (APN 7005-
  006-062) (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kristin Aguila, Advance Planning Manager.  A
  PowerPoint Presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments. Noting there were no
  individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed public comments and the public
  hearing.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to authorize the City
  Manager, or his designee, to execute, acknowledge, and consent to the sale of the
  subject property located at 13043 166th Street, Cerritos, California, 90703, in such
  form as the City Manager shall deem appropriate, including the Letter of Intent, a
  purchase and sale agreement, and all related escrow documents required or
  appropriate in connection with the completion of the sales transaction (COUNCIL). The
  motion carried (3 - 2) according to the following roll call vote:

  AYES:  Edwards, Pulido, Chen
  NOES:  Solanki, Ray
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of changes to the annual City Wide Pride Program
  (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Michael Yach, Management Analyst.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Ray and seconded by Solanki, to approve the staff
  recommended modifications to the City Wide Pride Program as follows:
  1.) Nomination Process:
  a. Eliminate the seven judging areas and open nominations to the general
  public; and
  b. Accept nominations by form entry and digital photograph to the City web
  page, GoRequest smartphone application, or by calling the Code
  Enforcement Department; and
  c. Accept Code Enforcement personnel nominations; and
  d. Accept only nominated properties free of code violations; and
  e. Publish photographs on the City website with permission of the
  homeowner/caretaker.
 City of Cerritos  February 25, 2016
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 4 of 6

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9A.  (continued)

  2.) Recognition:
  a. Recognize 5 to 10 homeowners per month at the Property Preservation
  meeting and post to the City web site; and
  b. Nominated properties can only be recognized once a year; and
  c. Acknowledge City Wide Pride homeowners with a letter from the City
  Council.

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray, Chen
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and consideration of award of a contract for Cerritos Park East
  rubberized track resurfacing, Project No. 12797, Bid No. 1219-16 (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Fredy Bonilla, Assistant Civil Engineer.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Pulido, to:
  1. Authorize the use of available funds originally allocated for the Cerritos Park East
  facility renovations and Bettencourt playground surfacing for Project No. 12797:
  Cerritos Park East track resurfacing; and
  2. Award a contract in the amount of $136,990 for Cerritos Park East rubberized track
  resurfacing, Project No. 12797, Bid No. 1219-16, to Beynon Sports Surfaces, Inc.
  and reject all other bids; and
  3. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any project-related change
  orders (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray, Chen
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9C.  Review and consideration of a public artwork donation from Coreland
  Companies, as agent for Cerritos Plaza LLC, in accordance with the City of
  Cerritos policy for accepting donated artwork/collectibles for public display
  (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kathy Matsumoto, Assistant City Manager.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.
 City of Cerritos  February 25, 2016
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 5 of 6

9.  New and Old Business (continued)
9C.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Ray, and seconded by Solanki, to direct the City Manager
  to execute the “Deed of Gift” on behalf of the City of Cerritos (COUNCIL).  The
  motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray, Chen
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9D.  Review and consideration of a reservation process for use of the sand volleyball
  courts at Liberty Park (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Sherré Titus, Recreation Services Superintendent.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Ray, and seconded by Solanki, to adopt the Parks and
  Recreation Commission’s sand volleyball court reservation process as detailed in the
  agenda report (COUNCIL). The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray, Chen
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

10.  Legislative Items

10A.  Report on pending legislation

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or
  Federal Legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.

  None.

11.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings

  Reports were provided by Councilmembers Pulido, Solanki and Edwards, Mayor
  Pro Tem Ray, and Mayor Chen.

  CONSENSUS (Solanki): Direct the City Manager to provide a report on the
  Southern California Edison leased parking lot income and expenses for the last
  three years.
 City of Cerritos  February 25, 2016
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 6 of 6

12.  Closed Session
  None.
13.  Adjournment

  The meeting was adjourned at 8:17 p.m.

  ___/s/Brenda Cabrera______________
  Brenda Cabrera, Assistant City Clerk/
  Assistant Agency Secretary
